phase1_rulings.R-1_OPERATOR_s7_three_regimes: S-7 has THREE regimes, not two. Operator-ruled 2026-08-06 after the vertical measurement, because the charter's 'a 120-col fallback is required' is an operator-approved clause and the counterexample re-opens it CONSTRUCTIVELY - the requirement comes out larger, not deleted. (1) At/above the wide breakpoint (_DIFF_WIDE_MIN = 139, content units): run list beside full-width windows. (2) At 120: the list becomes an OVERLAY on a dedicated key, the window takes full width, and the 2 visible hex rows are an explicitly-accepted paginable viewport. (3) Below the threshold where even that fails: an EXPLICIT NOTICE naming the required width/height, instead of the silently empty panel shown today. The notice regime is entered on HEIGHT as well as width - that is the whole finding - so its threshold must be DERIVED as a normative allocation bound over the measured vertical budget, never hand-picked. Closes the architect's OQ-1.
phase1_rulings.R-2_keyboard_arrows_enter: S-5's keyboard path is ARROWS + ENTER, bound on the LIST WIDGET, not the App. Taken by me. j and p are frozen in _PRE_BATCH_BINDINGS under live TC-011; k is a show=True footer chip for the Legend; only n is free App-level. Matches batch-77 ruling R3 verbatim, which dropped j/k/o for the identical reason - the second time this project has had to strike chartered keys against the same frozen guard.
phase1_rulings.R-3_s9_enter_open_in_hex_OUT: S-9's 'Enter posts an open-in-hex message' is OUT, on the architect's evidence: the existing handler renders current_file, which is generally NEITHER compared image, so it would silently show the wrong bytes. That is a defect, not a feature. Carried as C-78-d. The rest of S-9 (Footer + ? keymap discoverability) stays IN - the keyboard path is useless undiscovered.
phase1_rulings.R-4_increment_order_lane2_first: Lane 2 FIRST, Lane 1 LAST. Taken by me, and it resolves a direct contradiction between the two lanes rather than averaging it. The architect's D-10 (Lane 1 first, because the result area is structurally invisible) and QA's C-30 (Lane 2 first, for snapshot coverage) cannot both hold. MEASURED: the diff result area is ALREADY VISIBLE TODAY at 132x44 with 7 hex rows, so Lane 2's acceptances are observable with zero Lane 1 work - they are simply written at 132x44 instead of 120x30. That removes the architect's premise for ordering, leaving QA's, which is decisive: S-1 drifts 29 of 29 golden cells while Lane 2 drifts 1, so Lane 1 first would xfail 28 cells from increment 1 and ship all of Lane 2 with no snapshot coverage. EXCEPTION made explicit in the increment table: S-7's fallback and notice acceptances depend on S-8 AND S-1, so those specific ATs land Lane-1-side.
phase1_rulings.R-5_footer_coordinate_space: THE FOOTER FIGURE IS 8/13/15, NOT 7/12/14 - settled by my own execution after three honest parties produced three different numbers, which in this project means the TERM IS UNDEFINED rather than that someone cannot count. Footer.region.x == 1, so the document reading compares an ABSOLUTE x against a RELATIVE width, mixing coordinate spaces and silently discarding the right-aligned child that ends flush with the edge. Measured: (x - Footer.x) + w <= Fw gives 8/13/15 at 80x24 / 120x30 / 160x40; absolute x + w <= Fw gives 7/12/14. The architect was right; QA conceded the point but conceded to the WRONG NUMBER. NOTE THE CLASS: this is a UNITS error, identical to _DIFF_WIDE_MIN content-units-vs-terminal-width which this batch already fixed as M6 - the fix landed at one site and the LESSON did not propagate. Disposition: the requirement must state the COORDINATE SPACE and inclusion rule NORMATIVELY and derive the number from it, never swap 7 for 8. At 160x40 reading A gives 15 of 15, so none-truncated is TRUE there and the origin/main false-fail is about 8 of 15 at 80x24.

phase3_carries.C-78-v: A partial revert of a multi-declaration change mutates one of N co-dependent subjects whose token has changed denotation - record the value the declaration RESOLVED TO on the pre-change tree.
phase3_carries.C-78-viii: An applied-check proves a substitution happened, never that it is the one you meant. The missing limb is: the OLD token is absent after the write. (No LF/CRLF story - that baseline was contaminated by the reviewer own git show redirect, and the reviewer withdrew it.)
phase3_carries.C-78-ix: A defect class with no node is invisible however many nodes exist: 22 nodes were structurally blind to the second Compare.
phase3_carries.C-78-x: Analysing the right mechanism and deriving the WRONG CONSEQUENCE CLASS is a distinct failure mode from not having looked. The hazard was a stale MOUNT, not a stale READ.
phase3_carries.C-78-xi: enum.py tracked terms do not cover section 7 file-map cells, which is why the false C-21 discharge survived. Trace a miss to the CONTROL, not the person.
phase3_carries.C-78-xii: pause() is not a completion wait. It waits for queue idleness; a handler parked on an await has already dequeued its message.
phase3_carries.C-78-xiii: Pair the absence clause in the DRIVER, not the node - then the un-rendered state is unreachable by nodes NOT YET WRITTEN. Padding buys margin; a completion signal buys determinism.
phase3_carries.census_is_a_sample: A perturbation census reports a SAMPLE, not a set: arm A gave 12/14/15/15/14 across five runs on one host. The verdict rests on control >> 0 and discharge == 0, never on the count.
phase3_carries.C-78-i_ii_iii_iv_vi_vii: Inc-0/Inc-1 carries: the gitignored artifact path in section 7; LLR-121.2 fixture-less digest recipe; my brief-vs-spec divergence; the A/B Select width-1 defect (pre-existing on origin/main); section 5.1 rule 1 metric (BLOCKS Inc-10); the guard-placement rule needing after the SUBSTANTIVE assertions.
phase3_carries.F9: Duplicated Compare-driver and run-list helpers across the two test modules - one helper, not two. Batch-close item.
phase3_carries.C-78-xv: A declared mutation must be a value substitution that TYPE-CHECKS, or it is a wish. A mutation that raises goes red in the DRIVER, so the assertion never runs and it is not a discharge.
phase3_carries.C-78-xvi: A completion wait must be armed on an EDGE - and so must every clause that consumes its result. Inc-3 shipped that defect twice, ten lines apart: its len(written_md) == 1 silently encoded "the destination started empty".
phase3_carries.C-78-xvii: A newly minted wait owes the C-78-xii census on ITSELF, control arm mandatory.
phase3_carries.C-78-xviii: A measured figure is re-derivable only with the INCREMENT it was measured at, not merely the commit. Re-deriving against the wrong tree state reproduces nothing and looks like a contradiction.
phase3_carries.C-78-xx: OWED AN OWNER, and it is process work rather than an increment: every gate invoked through a pipe takes the PIPELINE exit status, not the gate. It fails silently in the SAFE-LOOKING direction. The orchestrator did exactly this and committed over a FAILING gate. Preferred fix: move the gate into the RC-1 pre-commit hook so shell plumbing cannot arbitrate a verdict.
phase3_carries.C-78-xxii: C-78-xv caught a declared MUTATION that was a wish; the same defect in a declared DISCHARGE is worse, because marking an assumed item discharged removes it from scrutiny PERMANENTLY. An assumed-verify-at-Phase-3 item is closed by a NODE, or it is not closed.
phase3_carries.C-78-xxiii: A mutation that reddens proves only that the one you picked was visible. When a clause tests a MAPPING, mutate to the IDENTITY, not to nothing - mutating to nothing breaks even an implementation that never uses the mapping. Measured: label->empty reddened the pre-fix node, label->identity would not have.
phase3_carries.proximity_confers_nothing: A citation copied from a document IN THE SAME PARAGRAPH that corrects a neighbouring citation is still uncorrected. One was re-derived because it was the subject; the neighbour was copied because it was only context.
